frozen_candidate_root_contribution: The root sbl contributes the notion of a WAY: a determinate, extended, traversable course/route that links a mover to a destination — something one goes along, is led along, opens, straightens, follows, or is barred from — and, by natural extension of the same conduit-image, the open avenue or means by which one proceeds toward an outcome. The root supplies only the traversable-course itself; it is normatively neutral (the way's rightness or wrongness, its physical vs. figurative destination, and its direction are all added by the genitive/preposition/context, not by sbl).

internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Every one of the 176 tokens is the substantive سبيل/سبل. The most transparent occurrences anchor the core as a concrete traversable route: God places rivers "and ways" (سبلا) in the earth so people may find their way (16:15), makes "ways" for them in it (20:53, 43:10), broad mountain passes as ways (فجاجا سبلا 21:31, 71:20); the bee is told to travel "the ways of your Lord" (سبل ربك 16:69); the lost fish "took its way into the sea" (اتخذ سبيله في البحر 18:61, 18:63); Lot's ruined town lies "by a way still standing" (لبسبيل مقيم 15:76). Here sbl = physical road/route, undeniably a traversable course. From this concrete anchor the same image extends, with the destination becoming a goal or standard rather than a place: 'the way' one is guided to (هديناه السبيل 76:3; يهدي السبيل 33:4; ثم السبيل يسّره 80:20), the way of right-conduct vs. the way of error (سبيل الرشد / سبيل الغي 7:146; سبيل الرشاد 40:38), the even/middle way (سواء السبيل 2:108, 5:12). Crucially the root stays normatively neutral: it attaches equally to the way of God (فى سبيل الله, dozens of times), the way of the criminals (سبيل المجرمين 6:55), of the corrupters (سبيل المفسدين 7:142), and 'the ways' one is warned NOT to follow (لا تتبعوا السبل 6:153) — so 'rightness' is not in sbl but in the genitive. The dense 'fī sabīl Allāh' frame (fighting 2:190, spending 2:195, migrating 4:100, striving 9:20) reads as motion/effort ALONG God's course. The negative-motion frame — barring from the way (صدوا عن سبيل الله 16:88), leading astray from it (ليضل عن سبيله 14:30), going astray from it (ضل عن سبيله 53:30) — presupposes exactly a course that can be traversed or diverted from. The traveler is 'son of the way' (ابن السبيل 2:177, 9:60) and the one merely 'crossing a way' (عابر سبيل 4:43) — persons defined by being on the road. Finally the 'means/recourse' cluster keeps the same conduit-image with an abstract terminus: 'is there any way OUT?' (هل الى خروج من سبيل 40:11), 'any way of return?' (الى مرد من سبيل 42:44), 'no way [of recourse]' (فما له من سبيل 42:46), and the liability idiom 'no way [of blame] against them / the way is against the wrongdoers' (ما عليهم من سبيل 42:41; السبيل على الذين 42:42; 3:75; 9:91,93), 'God will not grant the disbelievers a way over the believers' (سبيلا 4:141) — each is an avenue/route by which action or outcome may proceed. Across every family the invariant left after subtraction is 'a traversable course toward a terminus'.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: FORM: all 176 are one derivational form — the noun sabīl (pl. subul); there is no verb-form (I–X), participle, or maṣdar variation to subtract, so the root shows up purely as the concrete noun 'way'. CONSTRUCTION supplies the vector, not the root: fī+sabīl = motion/expenditure ALONG a course (fighting/spending/migrating fī sabīl Allāh); ʿan+sabīl = deviation/removal AWAY FROM the course (ṣadd, iḍlāl, ḍalāl ʿan sabīl); ilā...sabīl = a route TO a goal (sabīlan ilā rabbihi 25:57, khurūj min sabīl 40:11); ʿalā...sabīl = an avenue OF action against someone (sabīl ʿalā 42:42, 4:141). PARTICIPANTS vary wildly (God, believers, criminals, the bee, the fish, the wayfarer) and are irrelevant to the residue. CONTEXT (military, almsgiving, cosmological, eschatological, legal-liability) is likewise stripped. NORMATIVITY is constructional: attached to Allāh/rashād/salām it is good, to mujrimīn/ghayy/mufsidīn it is bad, so valence lives in the genitive, not in sbl. What survives every subtraction: a determinate traversable course/route connecting a mover to a terminus.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: The hardest cluster is the abstract liability/recourse idiom, especially 42:42 (إِنَّمَا ٱلسَّبِيلُ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يَظْلِمُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ — 'the sabīl is only against those who wrong people') and 3:75 (لَيْسَ عَلَيْنَا فِى ٱلْأُمِّيِّـۧنَ سَبِيلٌ — 'there is no sabīl against us regarding the gentiles'), plus 4:141 (a sabīl 'over' the believers) and 4:34 (do not seek a sabīl 'against' them). Here sabīl denotes grounds/entitlement-to-proceed, with no physical road and an abstract terminus (blame, dominance). It reconciles because the construction ʿalā/against + sabīl preserves the exact conduit-structure: an OPEN AVENUE/ROUTE by which action may proceed toward someone — negated ('no route of claim exists') or asserted ('the route of liability lies against the wrongdoers'). The internal bridge is attested within the same idiom-space: 40:11 'is there any way OUT (min sabīl)?' is a near-literal route-of-egress, and 42:44 'any way of RETURN' the same; the liability cases are just that route-to-outcome with the outcome being an act rather than a place. So the traversable-course image is recoverable, not forced.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: The strongest alternative is that sbl's core is 'the RIGHT/normative way (moral course)' — attractive given the overwhelming 'sabīl Allāh' frequency. Internal evidence decisively arbitrates against it: sbl attaches to plainly non-normative or evil courses — sabīl al-mujrimīn (6:55), sabīl al-mufsidīn (7:142), sabīl al-ghayy (7:146), and the plural subul one is commanded NOT to follow (6:153) — and to purely physical roads with no moral content (16:15, 20:53, 71:20, 18:61). Since the same root carries both good and bad ways, normativity must be supplied by the genitive/context, and the root residue reduces to normatively-neutral 'way/route'. A second alternative, core = 'means/instrument' (like sabab), is defeated by the abundant TRACK imagery — following it, straying off it, straightening it, barring people from it, a road 'still standing' (15:76) — which is spatial-traversal, not bare instrumentality; the means/recourse readings are a derived extension of the route-image, not its center.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Nearest neighbors: (1) ṣrṭ صراط 'the (one) straight highway' — internally contrasted with sbl in 6:153 (هَٰذَا صِرَٰطِى مُسْتَقِيمًا ... وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا۟ ٱلسُّبُلَ, the singular ṣirāṭ set against the branching subul) and 5:16 (سُبُلَ ٱلسَّلَٰمِ then صِرَٰطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ): ṣirāṭ is singular, grand, uni-directional; sbl is countable and pluralizable (subul), can branch, can be one's own or another's, can be good or evil, and can shade into 'means/access' — none of which ṣirāṭ does. (2) sbb سبب 'means/link/rope/cause' — pure instrumental connection with no traversal-track image; sbl always retains the go-along-a-course image. (3) hdy هدى 'guidance' — the process of directing, whereas sbl is the object/course TO which one is guided (hadaynāhu al-sabīl 76:3). (4) ṭrq طريق 'way/road' — closest gloss-synonym, but not attested here to arbitrate. FALSIFIABILITY: the analysis fails if a confirmed occurrence uses sabīl with a sense of pure abstract means/cause carrying NO recoverable route-toward-terminus image AND resisting the literal→figurative bridge (e.g. sabīl meaning simply 'reason/because' with no directional/avenue structure); no such case occurs in the 176.
internal_discovery.rationale: A single non-empty contribution — 'traversable course/route toward a terminus' — is recoverable in all 176 tokens without forcing. It is surface-anchored by numerous literal roads (rivers-and-ways, mountain-pass ways, the fish's course, the abiding road of 15:76) and holds through every extension by internally-attested bridges: the fī/ʿan/ilā/ʿalā constructions merely orient motion along, away from, toward, or against a course, and the metaphorical 'way of God', 'way of the criminals', and 'way/recourse against someone' all keep the conduit-structure intact. Direction is determinate (course linking mover to goal). The center is sharply distinct from ṣirāṭ, and the distinction is drawn by the text itself (6:153, 5:16), and from sabab (no track-image). Normative valence is demonstrably constructional, not rootal, since sbl labels evil ways too. The only inferential stretch is the abstract liability/recourse idiom (42:42, 3:75, 4:141), but it is bridged to the literal route-of-egress cases (40:11, 42:44) within the same idiom-space, so no occurrence is left unreconciled and none belongs in inconsistent_refs. Hence PREFERRED, and STRONG rather than MODERATE because the concrete route sense is abundant and the figurative uses remain transparently readable as 'way/avenue'.

adversarial_verification.notes: Adversarial sweep of all 176 tokens; all are the single noun سبيل/سبل = way/path/means. REFUTATION ATTEMPT: (1) Homonymy hunt — the root elsewhere yields 'ears of grain' (سنبلة) and 'downpour/draping' senses, which would break unity; NONE occur here (the سنابل in 2:261's verse-text is a different root; the token is سبيل الله). No semantic split to bridge. (2) Hardest cluster = the liability/recourse/dominance idiom (42:41, 42:42, 3:75, 9:91, 9:93, 4:34, 4:90, 4:141, plus way-out/return 40:11, 42:44, 42:46), where سبيل fades toward 'grounds/pretext/legal recourse/means of dominance.' I pressed for a genuine split but these resolve as the standard classical 'way/means of proceeding toward a terminus' (recourse reaching the wrongdoer; means of escape/dominance) — the candidate explicitly pre-folds this into 'the open avenue/means by which one proceeds,' so it is a recognized polyseme extension, saveable non-circularly, not a homonym. (3) Concrete roads (16:15, 20:53, 43:10, 21:31, 71:20, 16:69, 18:61/63, 15:76) anchor the core with zero stress; figurative-conduct and صد/ضل-عن frames presuppose a divertible course; fī-sabīl-Allāh = motion/effort along; ibn al-sabīl = person on the road. NEIGHBOR CONTRAST: the bare core does NOT discriminate against صراط (a near-synonym contrasted with subul in 6:153 and 5:16). Real discriminators: sbl pluralizes into diffuse سبل whereas SirāT is the single straight path, and sbl uniquely carries the cause/means/recourse frame (فى سبيل الله, ما عليه سبيل) that SirāT never takes — and since the candidate builds the means-extension into its contribution, it discriminates, moderately. Falsification condition (a token meaning grain-ear/downpour or otherwise non-way) is clear and unmet. No genuine failing occurrence found; unity distinct and falsifiable.
